title: HTML5 Form Validation & htmx:validation:failed Event Hooks

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Before sending a letter to the post office, the mailbox checks if you forgot the stamp (`required`) or wrote a fake email address (`type="email"`). If anything is missing, HTMX stops the letter from leaving and shouts `htmx:validation:failed` so you can show an error bubble without bothering the server.
progressiveExplaining.junior: HTMX natively honors standard HTML5 form validation attributes (`required`, `pattern`, `minlength`, `type="email"`). When a form or button with `hx-post` is submitted, HTMX calls `form.checkValidity()`. If invalid, the AJAX request is blocked and the browser displays native error bubbles. You can listen to `htmx:validation:validate` or `htmx:validation:failed` in JavaScript to attach custom validation rules.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, HTMX embraces the browser's native **Constraint Validation API**. When `htmx:validation:validate` fires, you can execute custom validation logic and set `evt.detail.error` or call `elt.setCustomValidity('error')`. If validation fails, HTMX cancels request dispatch, fires `htmx:validation:failed`, and halts the pipeline without network latency.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Before triggering an AJAX request, HTMX's `issueAjaxRequest` checks `element.checkValidity()`. If false, HTMX calls `element.reportValidity()`, dispatches the `htmx:validation:failed` event, and returns early. If custom validation logic in `htmx:validation:validate` calls `evt.preventDefault()` or assigns `evt.detail.valid = false`, the network request is aborted.

legacyOrBad.label: Custom JS Validation Engine
legacyOrBad.snippet: if (!validateRegex(email)) { showError(); return; } // ❌ Manual regex checks in JS

modernOrGood.label: Native HTML5 Validation with HTMX Hook
modernOrGood.snippet: <input type="email" required minlength="5" /> // ✅ NEW: Native constraint validation

fullFile.code:
<!-- ✅ NEW: Native HTML5 constraints checked automatically by HTMX before request -->
<form hx-post="/api/register" hx-target="#feedback">
  <input 
    type="email" 
    name="email" 
    required 
    minlength="5"
    placeholder="user@example.com"
  />
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

<script>
  // Custom dynamic rule hook:
  document.body.addEventListener('htmx:validation:validate', (evt) => {
    if (evt.detail.elt.name === 'email' && evt.detail.elt.value.endsWith('@banned.com')) {
      evt.detail.elt.setCustomValidity('Domain not allowed');
    }
  });
</script>

interviewGotchas.question: How can you disable client-side HTML5 validation and force HTMX to submit invalid forms directly to the server?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of server-side-only validation workflows.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Add the standard HTML5 **`novalidate`** attribute to the `<form>` element (or `hx-validate="false"` on the element). This causes HTMX to skip `checkValidity()` checks and submit the form data to the server immediately, allowing server-side validation to return formatted error messages in HTML.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Without `novalidate`, the browser will prevent submission and show native tooltips, preventing the server from receiving the invalid input.

interviewGotchas.question: What event is fired if you want to format custom error styling when validation fails in HTMX?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of HTMX lifecycle event listeners.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Listen to the **`htmx:validation:failed`** event: `document.body.addEventListener('htmx:validation:failed', (evt) => { evt.detail.elt.classList.add('is-invalid'); })`. This allows you to apply custom CSS classes and UI error badges whenever validation blocks a request.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Remember to remove the error class on `htmx:validation:validate` when the user corrects their input.
